subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw expose a core, agent-invocable compaction deferral/checkpoint contract, or keep continuity behavior in plugins using the existing lifecycle hooks?
rationale: Current hooks can support plugin experimentation, but the requested agent-controlled deferral changes session lifecycle and can affect what work or authority survives a compaction boundary.

options.title: Design a bounded core contract
options.body: Specify expiry, maximum deferrals, auditing, retry semantics, checkpoint scope, and explicit non-transfer of authorization before implementing a narrow API.

options.title: Prototype as a plugin
options.body: Use the existing compaction lifecycle hooks to validate checkpoint and recovery ergonomics without adding public core configuration or authority semantics.

options.title: Decline deferral, improve flush guidance
options.body: Keep compaction non-deferrable and limit core work to safer warnings or memory-flush improvements if maintainers do not want agents to influence the lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Specify expiry, maximum deferrals, auditing, retry semantics, checkpoint scope, and explicit non-transfer of authorization before implementing a narrow API.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction/defaults work and the current product boundary make this the strongest available routing candidate.
